Flora and Fauna of the Wealdwoods
Howling Beneath The Canopy
A long, under-slung jaw and extendable dewlap allows 
the lizard to quickly grab bird eggs from the nest and 
escape before attempting to swallow the large meal. 
While incapable of true flight, the reptile can weave and 
turn through the sprawl of branches and leaves with an 
agile grace, evading the parent birds seeking vengeance 
Vibrantly white, razor-thin bristles rise from the beetle's 
back acting as a deterrent for predators from snatching them 
from the tree trunks. The thin fibers detach easily from the 
insect and slip under scales and tangle in hair, often causing 
an infection from the abrasive wound, leaving many larger 
animals to give the incabruss beetle a wide berth

The long dead bones of a feheena rests where it 
slept, sheltered until its last fatal night before 
becoming an unfortunate victim of hollow mold. 
The mold slowly spreads in dark quiet spaces in 
a soft carpet, dormant until the warmth of a 
creature stirs its spores to asphyxiate its guest. 
Becoming the ideal lure for flies that the spores 
will then latch onto
The skittish frondilli weaves between trunk to trunk, eyes wide, ears sensitive to the slightest snap of twig or exhaled breath of awaiting predators. Its 
leaf-like fur conceals it from most eyes, but not all. The basilospri glides from the branches above, alighting on each bough, the thick moss blanketing 
each branch muffles its landing as it tracks the fleet-footed deer for the single deadly strike. With a blink of its scarlet eye, the reptile launches itself from 
above, aiding the pull of gravity as it shapes itself like an arrow, throwing its talons forward and aiming for the herbivore below. A wet snap and single 
cry of pain breaks the silence of an otherwise quiet afternoon beneath the leaves.
Under the overarching canopy of the Wealdwoods, life has learned to grow in tiers: From the scurrying underbrush, countless detrivores 
and fungi clear out the rot and detritus; from minute insects to the buried and colossal korrask, waiting for the right moment to kill. 
Above that, among the bushes crawl burberry beetles and crested quills within the understory, attempting to escape the grasp of an 
aphistus from pulling the thick leaves into its hungry beak. Among the winding hunting trails, a pack of vinnirex chase a lone scavick 
that leaps to the low hanging branches of a tree and soon enters a new tier of life. Among the trunks and branches in the canopy, dozens 
of feet above the ground live untold birds, climbing reptiles and small furred mammals. Smartest among those are the calitross, their 
flock ever keeping a wary eye out for the bladed talons of both basilospri and skyelarx that fly from branch to branch looking to pounce. 
Higher still, live those rare few that can witness the sky peeling through the thick leaves of the emergent layer. Green scaled ynnil perch 
on thin branches awaiting the pass of birds, and lexati glide elegantly on thermals, sunlight dappling their furred wings. These tiers 
offer a balance in the Wealdwoods not seen in other biomes, clear distinctions of place and purpose, until of course the earth shaking 
tread of its apex predator tears the colossal trees to the ground, exposing large swaths of the forest floor to streaking sunlight for the 
first time in decades and upending the rigid structure once more.
